transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
A day after the board of chipmaker Nvidia restored Jensen Huang to the CEO's post,
Attorney General Todd Blanche sidestepped questions about any Justice Department investigation
into Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and potential export control violations.
I don't know what you're speaking about some export investigation,
but we have a lot of investigations going on.
And by the way, I can't predict the future.
During a Tuesday news conference, Blanche called Nvidia a good corporate citizen
and said if Nvidia were the target of a criminal investigation,
that would not be the Trump administration's message to the public.
On Monday, President Trump said Huang had been exonerated.
However, questions from lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are swirling
after Trump took credit for Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia.
Kilmar Abrego-Garcia has self-deported.
The Salvadoran immigrant became a symbol of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown
after he was wrongfully deported and then brought back to the U.S.
and Piers Juliana Kim reports.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen wrote on "X" that "Kilmar is traveling to a country of his choice,
a free man, unharmed and with dignity."
The Democrat has played a leading role in championing Abrego-Garcia's case since last year
when the man who had been living in Maryland was deported to El Salvador by mistake.
The details of Abrego-Garcia's voluntary departure are unclear,
but it comes after months of sparring with the Trump administration.
Abrego-Garcia said he was willing to move to Costa Rica,
but the federal government did not support those plans and instead sought to deport him to a country in Africa.
Juliana Kim, NPR News.
King Tides flooded low-lying areas along the California coast Tuesday
from member station KQED in San Francisco, as were David Romero reports.
At over eight feet, King Tides pushed San Francisco to break a monthly record
for the highest tide ever in November.
That's partly because El Nino raised local sea levels a foot or more.
Wednesday's tides are forecast to be even taller
and could come close to its all-time record setback in 1983.
But even taller tides are expected around Christmas.
Here's San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie.
I want everybody to enjoy Thanksgiving, but we expect more rain in the coming months
and these King Tides are only going to get higher.
City officials were worried that storms would compound the flooding Wednesday,
but it looks like the storm will miss the King Tide window.
For NPR News, I'm Ezra David Romero in San Francisco.
Forecasters say King Tides could also cause coastal flooding in South Florida from Palm Beach to Miami
and that water levels could remain elevated for several hours before and after high tide Wednesday and Thursday.
You're listening to NPR News.
North Korea is expelling a Swiss diplomat, North Korea's Foreign Ministry said Wednesday
that the head of Switzerland's diplomatic office had been declared persona non grata
and has been ordered to leave the country within 48 hours.
In a statement, the Foreign Ministry said the expulsion was in response to Switzerland's decision
to add a North Korean international children's camp to its sanctions list.
For the many of us who can't afford a ticket to the Super Bowl and don't especially relish watching the event on TV,
there is a third option.
NPR's Chloe Veltman reports that IMAX theaters will be screening the big game for the first time ever in February.
ESPN's telecast of the Super Bowl on Valentine's Day next year
will be screened across hundreds of IMAX locations across the United States.
Football fans in some international markets, such as Australia, New Zealand and Brazil,
will be able to watch the action on IMAX's massive screens too.
The four-hour-long presentation will include a telecast of the main game,
the halftime show headlined by hip-hop artist Jay-Z, and pre-game and post-game coverage.
The Walt Disney Company, which is organizing the event alongside IMAX ESPN and the NFL,
calls the upcoming screening a milestone in cinema and the largest live event in IMAX history.
IMAX theater tickets for Super Bowl 61 are expected to go on sale in January.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
Tech stocks giving back some of their gains sparked by Jensen Hwang's return to NVIDIA
shares in the chip-heavy markets of South Korea and Taiwan down as much as 5 percent.
Japan's Nikkei share average down around 3 percent after Wall Street retreated Tuesday.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.
[♪upbeat music♪]

topics.text: Attorney General Todd Blanche sidesteps questions on Justice Department probe of Nvidia's Jensen Huang
Kilmar Abrego-Garcia self-deports after months of sparring with Trump administration
King Tides flood California coast, with San Francisco breaking its monthly tide record
North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in retaliation for Swiss sanctions on children's camp
IMAX theaters to screen the Super Bowl for the first time in February
Tech stocks fall after Wall Street retreat, with Korean, Taiwanese, and Japanese shares down
